name: Mattathias (priest, father of the Maccabean Revolt)
title: Father of the Maccabean Revolt
summary: Mattathias was a Jewish priest from Modi'in who started the Maccabean Revolt against the Seleucid Empire and their oppression of Jewish religious practice. He refused to sacrifice to Greek gods and killed both a Jew who intended to make such a sacrifice and the royal official. His sons, especially Judas Maccabeus, continued the fight for freedom after his death.

keyEvents.title: Refuses to Sacrifice to Idols
keyEvents.description: When royal officials came to Modi'in to force the Jews to sacrifice to Greek gods, Mattathias refused despite offers of honor and reward.

keyEvents.title: Killing the Apostate Jew and the Royal Official
keyEvents.description: When another Jew stepped forward to offer sacrifice, Mattathias was seized with zeal, killed him at the altar, and also killed the royal official.

keyEvents.title: Fleeing to the Mountains and Starting the Revolt
keyEvents.description: After this act, Mattathias cried out in the city that all who were zealous for the law should follow him, and he fled to the mountains with his sons.

keyEvents.title: Deciding to Fight on the Sabbath
keyEvents.description: After a group of Jews was massacred because they refused to defend themselves on the Sabbath, Mattathias and his followers decided to fight even on the day of rest.

keyEvents.title: Mattathias' Farewell Speech and Death
keyEvents.description: On his deathbed, Mattathias gave a speech in which he urged his sons to be zealous for the law and appointed Judas Maccabeus as commander.
